pharm: Thioxanthene antipsychotic; dopamine D1/D2 receptor antagonist with antipsychotic and, at low dose, antidepressant effects
quick: Oral 3-9 mg/day (max ~18 mg/day); depot decanoate 20-40 mg IM every 2-4 weeks
Take oral doses without regard to meals; avoid late-day dosing (alerting)
Avoid unless essential; neonatal extrapyramidal/withdrawal effects possible
Small amounts in milk; avoid or monitor infant
Use with caution; consider dose reduction
Use with caution; reduce dose in impairment
Avoid; additive sedation and CNS depression
Extrapyramidal symptoms, mental state, weight, metabolic profile, ECG/QT
summary: Flupentixol is a thioxanthene antipsychotic used for schizophrenia and other psychoses, available as oral tablets and as a long-acting depot (flupentixol decanoate) for maintenance. At low doses (flupentixol dihydrochloride) it has been used as a short-term treatment for depression in some countries. It blocks dopamine receptors and carries the typical risks of extrapyramidal effects and tardive dyskinesia. It is not FDA-approved; information reflects EMA/SmPC and BNF sources.
indications: Maintenance treatment of schizophrenia and other psychoses, particularly with apathy and withdrawal (oral and depot forms)
Short-term treatment of depression (low-dose flupentixol, in countries where licensed) as a second-line option

dosage.d: Initially 3 to 9 mg daily in divided doses, adjusted to response; usual maximum about 18 mg daily
dosage.t: Avoid dosing after 4 pm because of a mild alerting effect

dosage.d: Test dose 20 mg; then 20 to 40 mg every 2 to 4 weeks, adjusted to response (higher doses occasionally needed)
dosage.t: Deep intramuscular injection into the gluteal muscle
dosage.n: Give a small test dose first to assess sensitivity

dosage.d: 0.5 to 1 mg in the morning; maximum about 3 mg daily; if no response in 1 week, discontinue
dosage.n: Short-term use only; not a first-line antidepressant

dosage.d: Use a quarter to half the usual adult dose
dosage.n: Greater sensitivity to extrapyramidal and hypotensive effects

admin: Give a small test dose of the depot before the first full dose to detect hypersensitivity or extrapyramidal effects
Administer the depot by deep intramuscular injection, rotating sites
Avoid oral doses in the late afternoon or evening because of a mild alerting/activating effect
Titrate gradually and use the lowest effective dose, especially in the elderly
Withdraw gradually after long-term treatment to avoid rebound symptoms
moa: Flupentixol is a thioxanthene that blocks postsynaptic dopamine D1 and D2 receptors in the central nervous system, producing antipsychotic effects on positive symptoms of psychosis. It also has activity at adrenergic, serotonergic, and histaminergic receptors. At low doses it may exert a mild activating/antidepressant effect, possibly through presynaptic dopamine autoreceptor effects increasing dopaminergic transmission.

absolute: Comatose states or marked CNS depression (including alcohol, barbiturate, or opioid intoxication)
relative: Cardiovascular disease and QT prolongation or risk factors
Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies
Excitable or overactive patients (activating effect may worsen agitation)
monitor: Full blood count if infection or fever

preg: There are limited data. Avoid use in pregnancy unless considered essential. Neonates exposed in the third trimester are at risk of extrapyramidal and withdrawal symptoms after delivery; monitor the newborn.
lact: Flupentixol is excreted in breast milk in small amounts. Avoid if possible, or monitor the breastfed infant for sedation and extrapyramidal effects.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment and consider a reduced dose, as clearance may be affected and patients may be more sensitive to adverse effects.
hepatic: Use with caution and consider dose reduction in hepatic impairment, since flupentixol is extensively metabolized by the liver. Avoid in severe impairment.

major: Other QT-prolonging drugs (additive risk of arrhythmia, including torsades de pointes)
CNS depressants including alcohol, opioids, and sedatives (additive sedation and respiratory depression)
minor: Adrenaline (epinephrine) may cause paradoxical hypotension due to alpha-blockade
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it potentiates CNS depression
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum prolactin and affect ECG (QT); pregnancy and antibody tests are generally unaffected

rare: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
emergency: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (high fever, rigidity, altered consciousness, autonomic instability) - stop drug and seek emergency care
Acute dystonia or severe extrapyramidal reaction - urgent treatment with anticholinergic
Signs of blood clot or sudden collapse/fainting - emergency care

monitoring: Extrapyramidal symptoms and tardive dyskinesia at each review
Mental state and response, including any worsening of agitation from the activating effect
Weight, fasting glucose, and lipids periodically
ECG/QT interval, particularly with cardiac risk factors or other QT drugs
Full blood count if signs of infection; prolactin if clinically indicated
counsel: Take the daily dose as prescribed and avoid taking it late in the day, as it can be slightly stimulating and disturb sleep
Do not drink alcohol and be careful driving until you know how it affects you
Report any uncontrolled movements, severe stiffness with high fever, or fast/irregular heartbeat
Do not stop the medicine suddenly; your doctor will reduce it gradually if it is to be stopped
Attend appointments for monitoring of weight, blood sugar, and heart tracing
pk: Oral antipsychotic effect develops over days to weeks; depot over the dosing interval
Oral peak plasma concentration about 3-8 hours; depot peaks within about 4-7 days
Oral elimination half-life about 35 hours; decanoate depot about 3 weeks
Depot provides clinical effect over 2 to 4 weeks per injection
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from light; do not freeze the depot
pearls: Not FDA-approved; information reflects EMA/SmPC and BNF sources
Available as oral tablets and as a long-acting decanoate depot for maintenance of schizophrenia
Has a mild activating/alerting effect - avoid evening doses and use cautiously in agitated patients
Give a depot test dose first; watch for extrapyramidal effects, tardive dyskinesia, and QT prolongation
Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis - avoid in that setting
missed: For oral flupentixol, take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is late in the day or nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it. For the depot injection, contact your clinic to arrange the injection as soon as possible; do not double doses.
overdose: Overdose may cause somnolence, extrapyramidal symptoms, hypotension, hypo- or hyperthermia, seizures, and QT prolongation with arrhythmias. Treatment is supportive with airway protection, cardiac monitoring, and management of extrapyramidal effects with anticholinergics; there is no specific antidote. Contact a poison control center.
